title: adsbdb / hexdb.io route accuracy: measured
description:
A measurement of how accurately free callsign-to-route lookup services resolve an aircraft's origin and destination, and of where that error actually lives.

The error is regional rather than a matter of database staleness. adsbdb is 27% correct on US domestic flights (95% CI 14-44%, n=30) and 79% correct across the other regions sampled (66-88%, n=52); the intervals do not overlap. Record age barely matters - Australian routes verified at 100% on database rows with a median age of 11.5 years. The US figure was independently replicated at 28.6% across 395 flights using filed FAA flight plans as the arbiter, an order of magnitude larger sample by a different method.

A geometric plausibility check is also measured: rejecting a route the aircraft's own position contradicts separates correct from incorrect answers roughly 8 to 1, validated on 395 flights it was not designed against.

Published here: the method, the scripts and aggregate statistics. Withheld: per-flight records, which would redistribute two restricted datasets.

Sampling is stratified rather than random, and several regional cells are small; both are stated in the README limitations.
